newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Credit Lyonnais posts 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: France's Credit Lyonnais posts 1996 profit.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais, the French bank that nearly collapsed under the weight of its lending excesses, reported Thursday a modest rise in net profit for 1996 and a big improvement in underlying performance.
The state-controlled bank, rescued twice by the government, said net profit rose to 202 million francs ($35.5 million) from a 1995 profit of 13 million francs ($2.28 million).

But pretax profit excluding one-time items tripled to 4.5 billion francs ($789.5 million) from 1.5 billion ($263.2 million) "reflecting the recovery across the group's businesses" and the impact of restructuring, it said.

"1996 marks a spectacular recovery in the profitability of Credit Lyonnais," said Chairman Jean Peyrelevade, who steered the bank's turnaround from virtual bankruptcy following an expansion binge in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
The upturn is bound to anger rivals who say taxpayers have paid for the bank's recovery. The total state expense for saving Credit Lyonnais is expected to top 130 billion francs ($22.8 billion).
Despite the strong performance, the bank will still need another big dose of public money to ready it for sale. The government hopes to privatise the bank in early 1999.
The improved underlying performance was driven by lower operating expenses helped by staff cuts and strong returns from financial services and capital market activities.
